newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African PPI seen stable at 8.4 pct y/y in June.
newsitem.headline: S.African PPI seen stable at 8.4 pct y/y in June.

text.p: Producer inflation would remain unchanged in June after slowing in May, Huysamer Stals economist Johan Rossouw said on Wednesday.
The Central Statistical Service said earlier that the producer price index (PPI) increased 0.9 percent month-on-month and 8.4 percent year-on-year compared with rises of 0.4 and 8.8 percent in April.
The data was in line with a Reuters consensus poll of economists which forecast an 8.4 percent annual rate.
Rossouw said he expected the annual rate to remain at 8.4 percent in June.

"This forecast is based on a month-on-month rate of increase of 0.58 percent flowing from an assumed 0.1 and 0.8 percent month-on-month increase in the imported and locally produced components respectively," Rossouw said.
Annual imported and local inflation were expected to rise 5.6 and 9.1 percent respectively.
"We are convinced that the PPI inflation cycle has reached its upper turning point, and we expect it to decline sharply to about 6.0 percent towards year-end," Rossouw said.
He added that his forecast for an average PPI inflation rate of 8.2 percent for the year remained unchanged.
